shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Job's reply opens with the vaya'an formula, וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.26.1) -- the MT frame this row and the rest of the part follow through the third-cycle disarray of chapters 25-28. A PE mark precedes this opening, following Bildad's own close at Job.25.6 (oshb:Job.25.6 (petuchah, single-witness)). What follows is direct, second-person sarcasm aimed at Bildad: “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!” (web:Job.26.2; מֶה עָזַ֥רְתָּ לְלֹא כֹ֑חַ ה֝וֹשַׁ֗עְתָּ זְר֣וֹעַ לֹא עֹֽז, oshb:Job.26.2) and “To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came out of you?” (web:Job.26.4; אֶת מִ֭י הִגַּ֣דְתָּ מִלִּ֑ין וְנִשְׁמַת מִ֝י יָצְאָ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ, oshb:Job.26.4). The finite verbs addressed to Bildad in Job.26.2-Job.26.4a are second-person (עָזַ֥רְתָּ, ה֝וֹשַׁ֗עְתָּ, יָּ֭עַצְתָּ, הוֹדָֽעְתָּ, הִגַּ֣דְתָּ); the frame verbs of Job.26.1 are third-person wayyiqtols, and the relative clause of Job.26.4b (יָצְאָ֥ה, agreeing with its interrogative subject) is third-person feminine, with just the trailing מִמֶּֽךָּ carrying second person. The direct address to Bildad ends at Job.26.4, before the person shift to third-person cosmology at Job.26.5.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending Job's direct rebuke of Bildad through verse 14 instead of marking a shift at the person change to third-person cosmology at Job.26.5.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Job's sarcastic rebuke addressing Bildad directly

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A topic-turn interrogative opens the row: “How then can man be just with God? Or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?” (web:Job.25.4), rendering וּמַה יִּצְדַּ֣ק אֱנ֣וֹשׁ עִם אֵ֑ל... (oshb:Job.25.4). The question presses by a fortiori comparison -- even the moon and stars lack purity in his sight (web:Job.25.5; הֵ֣ן עַד יָ֭רֵחַ וְלֹ֣א יַאֲהִ֑יל..., oshb:Job.25.5) -- before collapsing onto humanity: “How much less man, who is a worm, and the son of man, who is a worm!” (web:Job.25.6; אַ֭ף כִּֽי אֱנ֣וֹשׁ רִמָּ֑ה וּבֶן אָ֝דָ֗ם תּוֹלֵעָֽה, oshb:Job.25.6). A PE mark follows in the single-witness inventory (oshb:Job.25.6 (petuchah, single-witness)), and the vaya'an formula opens Job's reply at web:Job.26.1, so this row's close carries two independent kinds of corroboration even though the interrogative alone marks its own opening.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this a fortiori turn back into the opening doxology rather than treating Bildad's six verses as two strophes.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Purity argument descending from moon-stars to worms

next_row.boundary_rationale: The address shifts from second-person rebuke to a third-person catalog of God's cosmic power: the departed spirits beneath the waters (web:Job.26.5; הָרְפָאִ֥ים יְחוֹלָ֑לוּ מִתַּ֥חַת מַ֝֗יִם וְשֹׁכְנֵיהֶֽם, oshb:Job.26.5), Sheol and Abaddon uncovered before him (web:Job.26.6; עָר֣וֹם שְׁא֣וֹל נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָֽאֲבַדּֽוֹן, oshb:Job.26.6), the sea stirred by his power and Rahab struck through by his understanding (web:Job.26.12; בְּ֭כֹחוֹ רָגַ֣ע הַיָּ֑ם ובתובנתו וּ֝בִתְבוּנָת֗וֹ מָ֣חַץ רָֽהַב, oshb:Job.26.12 -- a ketiv/qere pair sits inside this verse, single-witness disclosure), then the heavens garnished and his hand piercing the fleeing serpent (web:Job.26.13; בְּ֭רוּחוֹ שָׁמַ֣יִם שִׁפְרָ֑ה חֹֽלֲלָ֥ה יָ֝ד֗וֹ נָחָ֥שׁ בָּרִֽיחַ, oshb:Job.26.13). The catalog closes on a gnomic reflection: “Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?” (web:Job.26.14; הֶן אֵ֤לֶּה קְצ֬וֹת... מִ֣י יִתְבּוֹנָֽן, oshb:Job.26.14). Two further ketiv/qere pairs (his way/his ways; his power/his mighty acts) sit inside this closing verse (single-witness disclosure: oshb:Job.26.14), and a SAMEKH mark follows it in the same inventory (oshb:Job.26.14 (setumah, single-witness)). This row out-argues the very dominion doxology Bildad opened with at web:Job.25.2-Job.25.3, at five times the length.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Attributing this cosmological catalog to Bildad's developing argument rather than to Job's ironic escalation of it.
next_row.literature_type_guess: God's cosmological power catalog ending whisper-saying

next_row.boundary_rationale: Job's mashal resumption opens with the vayosef formula, וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.27.1) -- the same wording, byte-for-byte, that reopens at web:Job.29.1 after the wisdom poem (sweep: 2 book-wide for this exact formula, byte tier: oshb:Job.27.1, oshb:Job.29.1), and per the MT frame this span governs everything through the end of chapter 28. The formula opens an oath of personal integrity: “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter” (web:Job.27.2; חַי אֵ֭ל הֵסִ֣יר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י הֵמַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי, oshb:Job.27.2), closing “Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me” (web:Job.27.5; חָלִ֣ילָה לִּי֮ אִם אַצְדִּ֪יק אֶ֫תְכֶ֥ם..., oshb:Job.27.5). Chapter 27 itself carries no PE or SAMEKH mark in the single-witness inventory -- a SAMEKH mark precedes this row's own opening, following Job.26.14 (setumah, single-witness), the mark closing the preceding cosmological catalog immediately before this oath begins -- so this row's internal edges rest on the formula and the oath's own asseverative particles rather than on mark corroboration.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the oath at the parenthetical aside in verse 3 instead of reading 27:1-6 as one continuous asseveration.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Job's self-imprecatory oath of personal integrity

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A deictic heading opens the row's final movement: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty” (web:Job.27.13; זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק אָדָ֖ם רָשָׁ֥ע עִם אֵ֑ל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת עָ֝רִיצִ֗ים מִשַּׁדַּ֥י יִקָּֽחוּ, oshb:Job.27.13) -- a verse carrying two paseq segs in the single-witness seg layer (oshb:Job.27.13 (paseq, single-witness)). The two-word deictic opening זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק is byte-identical to the closing verse of Zophar's second speech, oshb:Job.20.29 (זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק אָדָ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע מֵאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְנַחֲלַ֖ת אִמְר֣וֹ מֵאֵֽל, web:Job.20.29 “This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God”) -- sweep: 2 book-wide at byte tier, the object's only two members -- and the parallel continues into the second colon, where both verses open with וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת (skeleton sweep: 3 book-wide, adding Job.31.2). What follows catalogs that wicked man's ruin -- children, wealth, house, and life all swept away -- closing “Men will clap their hands at him, and will hiss him out of his place” (web:Job.27.23; יִשְׂפֹּ֣ק עָלֵ֣ימוֹ כַפֵּ֑ימוֹ וְיִשְׁרֹ֥ק עָ֝לָ֗יו מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ, oshb:Job.27.23). The register here is close to the wicked-man's-doom catalog Zophar built his second speech around, and the byte-twinned heading strengthens that reading as more than a loose thematic echo; yet the MT text carries no new speech formula at this seam -- the material stays inside Job's vayosef mashal from web:Job.27.1 rather than being reassigned to a friend.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating verses 13-23 as displaced Zophar material and re-attributing them outside the vayosef frame.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Wicked man's comprehensive ruin from wealth grave

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The oath's register turns from asseveration to imprecation: “Let my enemy be as the wicked. Let him who rises up against me be as the unrighteous” (web:Job.27.7; יְהִ֣י כְ֭רָשָׁע אֹ֣יְבִ֑י וּמִתְקוֹמְמִ֥י כְעַוָּֽל, oshb:Job.27.7), then to a question about that wicked one's standing: “For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?” (web:Job.27.8; כִּ֤י מַה תִּקְוַ֣ת חָ֭נֵף..., oshb:Job.27.8). The row closes turning back on the friends themselves: “Behold, all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?” (web:Job.27.12; הֵן אַתֶּ֣ם כֻּלְּכֶ֣ם חֲזִיתֶ֑ם וְלָמָּה זֶּ֝֗ה הֶ֣בֶל תֶּהְבָּֽלוּ, oshb:Job.27.12) -- a second-person plural rebuke closing the ring opened by the second-person singular taunt against Bildad at web:Job.26.2.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verses 7-12 as a continuation of the personal-integrity oath rather than as its own imprecatory turn. Separately, a live rival at the row's own back edge is recorded, not adopted: oshb:Job.27.11's אוֹרֶ֣ה אֶתְכֶ֣ם (“I will teach you”, web:Job.27.11) is the earliest second-person-plural address after Job.27.5 -- the 2mp object pronoun אֶתְכֶ֣ם sweeps 6 book-wide at skeleton tier (Job.13.9, Job.13.10, Job.13.11, Job.27.5, Job.27.11, Job.32.6), with Job.27.5 and Job.27.11 the members inside this mashal -- so Job.27.11-Job.27.12's direct teaching address to the friends could instead be read as the hinge introducing the deictic heading of Job.27.13 rather than as this row's own closing turn. The row's edge at Job.27.12|Job.27.13 stands on the independently attested heading formula at Job.27.13 (a two-word deictic opening, byte-identical to oshb:Job.20.29, sweep: 2 book-wide, with a shared second-colon echo וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת sweeping 3 book-wide (skeleton tier) -- Job.20.29, Job.27.13, Job.31.2; at byte/accent-stripped tier the count narrows to 2, Job.27.13 and Job.31.2 alone sharing this pointed spelling with meteg and merkha, while Job.20.29 carries the distinct accent-stripped form וְנַחֲלַ֖ת, meteg-less with tipeha), so the rival at Job.27.10|Job.27.11 is disclosed rather than adopted.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Imprecation turning to the godless's own destruction

next_row.boundary_rationale: No new speech formula opens chapter 28: the particle כִּ֤י יֵ֣שׁ ('surely there is', asseverative, oshb:Job.28.1) begins a mining excursus inside the same vayosef span that opened at web:Job.27.1, describing how miners break shafts for silver and gold “away from where people live” (web:Job.28.4). The row runs through techniques for extracting hidden treasure -- “He puts his hand on the flinty rock, and he overturns the mountains by the roots” (web:Job.28.9) -- closing “He binds the streams that they don't trickle. The thing that is hidden he brings out to light” (web:Job.28.11; מִ֭בְּכִי נְהָר֣וֹת חִבֵּ֑שׁ וְ֝תַעֲלֻמָ֗הּ יֹ֣צִא אֽוֹר, oshb:Job.28.11). A PE mark follows in the single-witness inventory (oshb:Job.28.11 (petuchah, single-witness)), and two paseq segs mark verses 3 and 4 within the row (oshb:Job.28.3 (paseq, single-witness); oshb:Job.28.4 (paseq, single-witness)).
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Marking a new top-level unit at 28:1 despite the absence of any speech-formula seam there.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Mining catalog seeking silver hidden underground

next_row.boundary_rationale: The wisdom poem's refrain opens the row at its earlier of two book-wide occurrences (sweep: 2 book-wide, skeleton tier: oshb:Job.28.12, oshb:Job.28.20): “But where will wisdom be found? Where is the place of understanding?” (web:Job.28.12; וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תִּמָּצֵ֑א וְאֵ֥י זֶ֝ה מְק֣וֹם בִּינָֽה, oshb:Job.28.12) -- the fronted, topicalized 'wisdom' breaking from the mining catalog's third-person miner-subject. What follows argues wisdom's price is beyond purchase: “It can't be gotten for gold, neither will silver be weighed for its price” (web:Job.28.15; לֹא יֻתַּ֣ן סְג֣וֹר תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ..., oshb:Job.28.15), running through onyx, sapphire, coral, crystal, and topaz before closing “The topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it. It won't be valued with pure gold” (web:Job.28.19). A PE mark follows in the single-witness inventory (oshb:Job.28.19 (petuchah, single-witness)), immediately before the refrain's second occurrence reopens the question in the row that follows (oshb:Job.28.20); another PE mark already precedes this row's own opening, following Job.28.11 (petuchah, single-witness), the mark closing the preceding mining excursus immediately before this price catalog begins.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Running the price catalog together with the preceding mining excursus as one long row instead of opening a new strophe at the refrain.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A spatial scene shift opens the row's stated content: “when I went out to the city gate, when I prepared my seat in the street.” (web:Job.29.7), moving Job's recollection from the tent and household of the row before it out to the public square. Grammatically, however, Job.29.7's opening בְּצֵ֣אתִי is the same ba-plus-infinitive-construct subordinate form as two that precede it inside the preceding row, Job.29.3 בְּהִלּ֣וֹ and Job.29.6 בִּרְחֹ֣ץ (Job.29.5's בְּע֣וֹד is a distinct bet-plus-substantive form on the free-standing adverb, not an infinitive construct, and does not belong to this chain), all depending on the wish of Job.29.2 -- so the subordinating chain continues across this row's own opening edge rather than breaking there, and the finite qatal narration that actually resumes the main clause (רָא֣וּנִי נְעָרִ֣ים וְנֶחְבָּ֑אוּ, “The young men saw me and hid themselves”) falls one verse later, at Job.29.8. That later seam is disclosed here as the row's own honest rival, not adopted: the chunked edge at Job.29.6|Job.29.7 rests on the content-scene shift to the city gate, which is real, while the syntactic subordination-chain break sits at Job.29.7|Job.29.8. The strophe catalogues the deference shown him there (young men hiding, elders standing, princes restraining speech, nobles' tongues sticking to the roof of the mouth) and then his own conduct as benefactor (deliverer of the poor, father to the needy, breaker of the unrighteous's jaws), holding together as one continuous public-honor tableau through Job.29.17 before a self-referential quotation frame reopens the material at Job.29.18.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: One could split the young-men/elders reaction (Job.29.8-Job.29.10) from the ear-and-eye testimony and benefaction catalogue (Job.29.11-Job.29.17) as two rows, but nothing marks a seam between them beyond a shift of grammatical subject within the same scene.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Job's justice deeds protecting fatherless and widow

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The vayosef verb reopens Job's voice (וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר) immediately after the wisdom poem's quotation frame at Job.28.28 (וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָֽאָדָ֗ם...) closes on the fear-of-the-Lord maxim; a Masoretic setumah follows Job.28.28 (oshb:Job.28.28 (setumah, single-witness)), weak corroboration sitting exactly where the new formula begins. The wording matches, byte for byte, Job's earlier resumption formula at Job.27.1 (וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר), marking this as a second, independent vayosef uptake rather than a continuation of the mashal begun there. The strophe itself opens on a longing formula, “Oh that I were as in the months of old” (web:Job.29.2), built on the one-word wish-verb יִתְּנֵ֥נִי (a mi-plus-suffixed-verb form, distinct from the two-word idiom attested 9 times elsewhere in the book, e.g. מִ֤י יִתֶּן at Job.31.35), and runs through images of divine favor, household intimacy, and agricultural plenty (lamp on the head, God's council over the tent, oil poured from the rock, Job.29.3-Job.29.6) that end at Job.29.6 as the content turns outward to the city gate at Job.29.7. That content turn is the row's stated closing warrant, not a syntactic one: Job.29.3 (בְּהִלּ֣וֹ) and Job.29.6 (בִּרְחֹ֣ץ) are ba-plus-infinitive-construct subordinate clauses depending on the wish of Job.29.2 -- Job.29.5's בְּע֣וֹד is a distinct bet-plus-substantive form on the free-standing adverb, not an infinitive construct, and does not join this pair -- and that same infinitive-construct pattern continues one verse past this row's own edge, at Job.29.7 (בְּצֵ֣אתִי, “when I went out to the city gate”) -- disclosed here rather than adopted as a redrawing, since the chunked span holds the content-scene shift as the seam and finite qatal narration does not in fact resume until Job.29.8 (רָא֣וּנִי, “The young men saw me”), one verse into the row that follows.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A rival reading folds Job.29.1 into the preceding wisdom-poem span since neither carries a vaya'an frame, but the vayosef verb itself is a distinct formula family and its wording duplicates Job.27.1's rather than Job.28's silence.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Job's nostalgic portrait of past prestige esteem

next_row.boundary_rationale: A self-referential discourse frame opens the row, וָ֭אֹמַר (וָ֭אֹמַר עִם קִנִּ֣י אֶגְוָ֑ע), “Then I said, ‘I will die in my own house, I will count my days as the sand.” (web:Job.29.18) -- one of 2 verse-initial vav-consecutive-imperfect-1cs tokens of this exact form book-wide (accent-stripped sweep: 2, Job.29.18 and Job.38.11; the two differ in their accents, so not byte-identical to each other), and the only one of the two spoken in Job's own voice as a self-quotation frame (Job.38.11's token sits inside the Job.38.1 YHWH speech-formula span). A wider skeleton-substring search over-collects to 4 by also catching two grammatically distinct forms sharing the same consonants: Job.22.13's perfect 2ms וְֽ֭אָמַרְתָּ (Eliphaz addressing Job, not a self-quotation) and Job.7.4's perfect 1cs וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי (word 3 of its verse, not verse-initial) -- this is the skeleton-is-substring-not-root hazard the toolkit documents. The row turns from the gate-scene catalogue to Job's private expectation of an unbroken future (nest, sand, spread roots, renewed bow). The strophe then returns, without a new formula, to public deference (“Men listened to me, waited, and kept silence for my counsel.” web:Job.29.21) and closes the chapter's reminiscence on the king-in-the-army, comforter-of-mourners simile, “I chose out their way, and sat as chief. I lived as a king in the army, as one who comforts the mourners.” (web:Job.29.25), the row's natural terminus before the adversative that opens Job.30.1.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: The private-confidence images of Job.29.18-Job.29.20 could stand as their own short row framed by the quotation verb, but nothing marks a return seam at Job.29.20|Job.29.21 comparable to the frame that opens Job.29.18, so the chapter's closing material is kept whole.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Job's hope of enduring blessing like renewed phoenix

next_row.boundary_rationale: וְעַתָּ֤ה (וְעַתָּ֤ה שָֽׂחֲק֣וּ עָלַי֮ צְעִירִ֥ים), “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision” (web:Job.30.1), opens the chapter's antithesis to Job.29 with the initial occurrence of three of this 'but now' marker that structure Job's present-misery complaint (sweep: 3 of 8 book-wide tokens of this marker fall in this chapter, at Job.30.1, Job.30.9, Job.30.16). The row describes the outcasts who now mock him -- their degraded origin, gaunt hunger, and expulsion from human company -- as one continuous third-person description that ends at Job.30.8, before the subject shifts to Job's own experience of their scorn at Job.30.9.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading Job.29.25|Job.30.1 as one continuous strophe is possible on parallelism grounds alone, but the adversative particle plus the reversal of content (from honored elder to mocked outcast) marks a genuine participant and register change, not mere texture.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Youth's mockery making Job their derision target

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: No new speech formula opens Job.31 -- it remains inside the Job.29.1 vayosef span -- but the genre shifts abruptly from lament to legal self-asseveration: בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י ..., “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?” (web:Job.31.1). The row states the covenant with the eyes and its rationale (calamity as God's portion for the wicked) as a four-verse prologue, closing on the rhetorical question “Doesn’t he see my ways, and count all my steps?” (web:Job.31.4), which sets up the opening conditional protasis at Job.31.5.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Job.31.1-Job.31.4 could be folded into the oath that follows (Job.31.5-Job.31.8) as its rationale clause rather than standing alone, but the covenant statement and its grounding question use no conditional particle at all, unlike the chapter's אם particle-token series, which sweeps 17 tokens over 17 verses from Job.31.5 to Job.31.39 (including the oath-affirmation אם לא at Job.31.36, itself not a protasis) -- a series that does not reach every strophe of the chapter, since Job.31.35 opens instead on the two-word wish idiom מִ֤י יִתֶּן with no conditional particle of its own.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: אַ֣ךְ, “However doesn’t one stretch out a hand in his fall” (web:Job.30.24), turns from direct address to a general maxim about compassion toward the fallen, then to Job's own record of weeping for the needy (Job.30.25), and closes the chapter with a return to self-directed lament -- blackened skin, burning bones, harp and pipe turned to mourning at Job.30.31, “Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the voice of those who weep.” (web:Job.30.31) -- a cadence that answers, in reverse, the counsel-and-comfort close of Job.29.25.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: The opening particle here is weaker than the chapter's three-times-repeated 'but now' marker, so an alternative keeps Job.30.24-Job.30.31 attached to the preceding direct-address block as its closing application rather than a fresh strophe.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Job's weeping for afflicted despite own anguish

next_row.boundary_rationale: The oath series proper begins: אִם הָלַ֥כְתִּי עִם שָׁ֑וְא ..., “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit” (web:Job.31.5), the opening member of a 17-token protasis-particle sweep spanning the rest of the chapter, to Job.31.39 (sweep: 17 book-wide-in-ch31). A second clause of the same particle follows at Job.31.7 ('if my step has turned out of the way'), and the pair resolves in one apodosis at Job.31.8 ('then let me sow, and let another eat'). A Masoretic petuchah follows Job.31.7 (oshb:Job.31.7 (petuchah, single-witness)) -- weak, non-driving corroboration that falls inside this protasis-apodosis unit rather than at its edge, and is disclosed without redrawing the row.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: The Masoretic petuchah (single-witness) after Job.31.7 might tempt a split before the apodosis at Job.31.8, but marks stay tier-3 corroboration in Writings and do not drive a boundary that would sever a protasis pair from the one apodosis answering both.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Oath against adultery's lust and marriage deception
